:::{#thm-double-exponential}
#### When repeated exponentiation is not reordered

Let $a \ge 0$ and $b, c \in \reals$, where $b^c$ is defined.
Then $(a^b)^c = a^{(b^c)}$, with both sides defined, if and only if

- $a > 0$ and either $a = 1$ or $bc = b^c$; or
- $a = 0$, $b \ge 0$, and $c > 0$.

:::

::: proof

This is the solution to @exr-double-exponential.

:::
